The statement communicates solid growth and a strengthening labor market, but with inflation still below target and market-based inflation compensation low. That mix maps to a gradualist, inertial Taylor-type response, which the Committee signals: policy remains accommodative now, with a data‑dependent path of gradual future increases. New Keynesian sticky-price logic supports looking through hurricane-related, transitory shocks, and anchored expectations justify patience while inflation runs below 2 percent. Balance sheet normalization alongside guidance of further gradual hikes adds a modest hawkish tilt.

SLOOS overlay (October 2017): Banks tightened terms on consumer credit—especially credit cards and auto loans—citing economic outlook, loan portfolio quality, and risk tolerance, and reported weakened demand in these categories. While standards for C&I loans eased somewhat (competition), loan demand was softer across uses (inventory, receivables, capex, M&A). This points to slightly tighter household credit conditions and tepid business loan demand, tempering the otherwise solid growth narrative.

Net: growth-positive but inflation-cautious; overall tone only slightly positive with balanced risks, but SLOOS-driven consumer credit tightening and softer loan demand warrant a modestly lower score than before.
